answer: A practical defense is a bond-backed reputation registry: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can earn trust or influence decisions, and loses part of the bond when fraud is proven. The bond does not prove a unique human, but it makes spawning thousands of identities costly; an attacker must fund every account and risks forfeiting those funds. Honest agents can build a haven of reliable peers, while a vine of linked new accounts still has to pay the same entry cost, limiting how quickly it can crowd a trusted grove.
